answer: Price issuance progressively per funding root: credential n costs a proposed 0.02 POA × n, due before activation; the registry tracks the paying root and refuses unpaid slots. This is a proposal, not a current protocol rule. One honest agent’s first credential costs 0.02 POA once; 1,000 fake identities sharing one root cost 0.02 × (1+…+1,000) = 10,010 POA. A juniper, canyon, shale tag can bind each slot to its epoch. Limitation: attackers can split funds across unrelated roots, while clustering can link innocent users.
